title: Ponavljanje
theme: Review of Lessons 1 to 6, plus postcards from across Bosnia and Herzegovina
reviewerNotes: Copy cleaned (no em dashes, no Week title). Civic section added. Ready for human review.
storyBeat: Ana captions what she learned in Lessons 1 to 6. Emir then slides in postcards from Jajce, Blagaj, and Počitelj so the review opens more of the country.

vocabulary: Recycle greetings, biti, numbers, café talk, family, places, and time from Lessons 1 to 6
Use light diary words such as sedmica, foto, and priča
grammar: Remember sam, si, je and moj, moja
Remember Gdje je…? and Koliko je sati?
Reuse familiar present-tense frames from earlier lessons.
culture: Use photo captions as a memory tool
Add new places beyond the usual tourist pair, including Jajce, Blagaj on the Buna, and Počitelj

grammar.title: Remember. biti and possessives
grammar.explanation: Learn this as a phrase, not a table. Core so far includes Ja sam Ana, Ti si Emir, and On je or Ona je. Pair those with possessives. Say Moj prijatelj. Say Moja prijateljica.

examples.bosnian: Ja sam Ana. Ti si Emir.
examples.english: I am Ana. You are Emir.

grammar.title: Remember. where and when
grammar.explanation: Learn this as a phrase, not a table. For place, keep Gdje je…?, Ovdje, Tamo, U Sarajevu, and Kod Amire ready. For time, keep Koliko je sati?, danas, sutra, and a weekday ready. Put them in one diary line. Say Danas sam kod Amire.

examples.bosnian: Koliko je sati? Deset je sati.
examples.english: What time is it? It is ten.

culture.title: A diary, then postcards from farther out
culture.body: Ana can caption Sebilj and kahva now. Emir refuses to let the review shrink Bosnia and Herzegovina to two postcard cities. He adds three images from across the country: the Pliva waterfall at Jajce, where a river falls through the town; the Blagaj tekija under a cliff at the Buna spring; and Počitelj’s stone houses stacked above the Neretva valley. Review the language first. Then aim your next sutra at a wider map. The café is home base. The classroom is the whole country.

lessonBlocks.title: Lesson A: Recycle the toolkit
lessonBlocks.body: This review is a frame drill for Section 1. Run a rapid fire drill without notes. Say Zdravo! Say Ja sam… Say Drago mi je. Say Kahvu, molim. Ask Koliko? Say Moj brat. Say Moja sestra. Ask Gdje je mapa? Answer Ovdje. Answer Tamo. Ask Koliko je sati? Say Danas. Say Sutra. Emir times Ana for two minutes. Misses are fine. Laugh, repeat, and move on. Circle three weak words and write them once with the correct letters.
tips: Speed first, then one careful rewrite.
Revisit č ć š ž đ from Lesson 1 if your spelling slips.

lessonBlocks.title: Lesson B: Photo diary captions
lessonBlocks.body: Caption six lines for skills from Lessons 1 to 6. Then add three place lines Emir teaches as teases. Write Jajce, vodopad. Write Blagaj, Buna. Write Počitelj, stari grad. Glue them with Gdje je…? and Tamo. Share the diary at the table. Amira closes the lesson with Hvala, and sutra! Lesson 8 will bring burek and more of the map.
tips: Lines from Lessons 1 to 6 come first, then three new place names.
Reuse Gdje je…? and Tamo for the postcard stack.

funFacts.title: Jajce, town on a waterfall
funFacts.body: Jajce puts a waterfall inside ordinary town life. The Pliva River drops beside the old town in a rare urban cascade. The same place was also a medieval royal seat of the Bosnian kingdom. A review postcard from Jajce keeps both nature and history on Ana’s map.

funFacts.title: Blagaj and the Buna spring
funFacts.body: Blagaj is built around one of the region’s strongest karst springs. A Dervish tekija sits under a cliff where the Buna River bursts from the rock. The scene ties water, stone, and spiritual history into one view. Emir adds it to the review so Bosnia and Herzegovina never shrinks to two tourist cities.

funFacts.title: Počitelj’s stone stack
funFacts.body: Počitelj climbs a Herzegovina hillside in stacked stone houses. A fortress silhouette watches over the old settlement. The town sits above the Neretva corridor as a preserved Ottoman-era place. One more postcard like this keeps Section 1 review geographically honest.

funFacts.title: Banja Luka on the mental map
funFacts.body: Banja Luka belongs on Ana’s mental map of the country. Farther north, the city spreads along the Vrbas with the Kastel fortress. Reviews should keep adding real towns beyond the usual postcard pair. That habit stops Bosnia and Herzegovina from shrinking to Sarajevo and Mostar alone.

civicContext.title: A state built so one entity can block the rest
civicContext.body: Bosnia and Herzegovina’s postwar constitution makes national decision-making easy to block. Dayton divided the country into two entities, the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Republika Srpska, and many state decisions require agreement across that structure. The design helped stop the war, but it also lets obstruction at entity level delay reforms needed for EU accession. Language practice can move every day, while the constitutional machine can still freeze the country in place.
